culture_principles.name: Helpful technology for everyone
culture_principles.description: Google-style impact should connect technical work to user usefulness, broad accessibility, and products that help many kinds of users.

culture_principles.name: Structured problem solving with clarity
culture_principles.description: Strong candidates clarify assumptions, decompose problems, reason through alternatives, explain trade-offs, test edge cases, and communicate while solving.

culture_principles.name: Googleyness and leadership through evidence
culture_principles.description: Behavioral strength is shown through collaboration, humility, ambiguity handling, influence without authority, conflict resolution, and learning.

culture_principles.name: Bold and responsible innovation
culture_principles.description: AI/product answers should combine ambition with safeguards, testing, monitoring, privacy, fairness, safety, and user trust.

culture_principles.name: Role-specific depth
culture_principles.description: Google lens should adapt by role: SWE coding, SRE reliability, Data Analyst metric validation, UI/frontend user experience, AI/ML evaluation and deployment.

hiring_signals.signal: Clarifies ambiguous problems before solving and explains assumptions, constraints, complexity, and edge cases.
Shows collaboration, humility, conflict handling, and influence without relying on formal authority.
For AI/product work, balances bold innovation with rigorous responsible-development controls.
Connects technical work to useful, inclusive, safe, and measurable user outcomes.
Adapts preparation and answers to role-specific expectations for SWE, SRE, Data Analyst, UI, Android, and AI/ML.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Jumping into implementation or code without clarifying the problem.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Google-style technical evaluation strongly rewards problem decomposition, assumptions, and communication while solving.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Memorized Googleyness language without concrete examples of collaboration, humility, conflict handling, or ambiguity.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Behavioral fit should be evidence-based, not personality polish.

anti_signals.anti_signal: AI/product answers that optimize model or product metrics while ignoring safety, privacy, fairness, monitoring, or user trust.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Google's AI principles make responsibility part of product quality.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Assuming interview performance alone guarantees offer or team match.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Candidate accounts describe hiring committee and team matching uncertainty; outputs should preserve process humility.

interview_patterns.pattern: SWE interviews should test DSA/problem solving, clarifying questions, complexity, tests, code quality, and narrated reasoning.
G&L / Googleyness interviews should test collaboration, leadership without authority, ambiguity, humility, conflict, and learning.
SRE interviews should test reliability thinking, debugging, automation, systems knowledge, communication, and user impact under incidents.
Data roles should test metric definition, data quality, analytical reasoning, stakeholder interpretation, and product/user impact.
AI/ML roles should test evaluation design, error analysis, responsible deployment, and user-facing quality beyond offline metrics.

honest_limits: This is a public-source and private-distillation draft lens and does not represent an official Google hiring standard.
Google Careers public pages exposed limited process detail in accessible HTML, so candidate-process patterns remain lower-confidence.
Private materials authorized by the project owner are included only as distilled aggregate patterns, not raw article text or copied questions.
Role, level, region, recruiter, hiring committee, and team matching can materially change candidate experience.
This v0.1 lens has static validation cases but is not approved for production screening until live answer backtesting and reviewer approval are complete.
This v0.2 lens has structured evidence records and an evidence audit, but is still not approved for production screening.
Public source URLs and private-material provenance must be reviewed before v1.0 approval.
